title: A second good option
hook: Would adding another attractive player make buying easier?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Show how choice conflict can change deferral while both options remain available.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Show how choice conflict can change deferral while both options remain available.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy choice has option A worth eight units at a cost of three. Adding B worth seven at a cost of three changes A’s net value to what? Toy inputs A=[8, 3, 0, 0]; B=[8, 3, 7, 3].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[5, 5, 0], [5, 5, 4]]. Labels: A net, Best net, B net.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Adding an alternative changes the choice set but leaves A’s stated payoff unchanged. A person may still defer when choices conflict; the arithmetic separates that behavioral response from removal or degradation of the original option.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Option A value=8, A cost=3, Option B value=7, B cost=3. What is A net? Answer: 5.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Option A value=8, A cost=3, Option B value=7, B cost=3. What is A net?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 5. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: With one good CD player on sale, 34% chose to wait; adding a second good option raised waiting to 46% (Tversky & Shafir, 1992).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Show how choice conflict can change deferral while both options remain available.
